newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND STRUGGLE IN SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND STRUGGLE IN SECOND TEST.

text.p: England were in trouble at lunch on the opening day of the second test against Zimbabwe at Harare Sports Club.
Put into bat the tourists were reduced to 63 for three in the morning session. Nasser Hussain was on seven with Graham Thorpe on five.

On a steamy morning with the ball swinging about Nick Knight was the first to go. Shaping to leg glance paceman Henry Olonga's first ball, Knight got a thin edge through to wicket-keeper Andy Flower when he had made 13.
Mike Atherton was lucky to survive a top edge from a short ball from Eddo Brandes. The ball looped down to fine leg where Guy Whittall got a hand to the ball, but couldn't prevent it going for six.
But when Atherton had made 15 he drove loosely at a wide ball from Whittall and edged to Alistair Campbell at first slip.

In the previous over from Heath Streak, Campbell had dropped a simple chance from Alec Stewart, but it did not cost Zimbabwe anything. In Streak's next over Stewart drilled a cover drive straight to Grant Flower to be caught for 19.

England made one change from the side which drew in Bulawayo, with newly arrived all rounder Craig White coming in for Chris Silverwood. Zimbabwe made two changes with left hand bat Mark Dekker replacing Stuart Carlisle and seamer Eddo Brandes coming in for Bryan Strang.
